extracted.intended_audience: sovereigns, statesmen, political philosophers, and educated readers/students of political theory
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpts from Hobbes' Leviathan giving principles and practical standards for sovereign government, punishment, rewards, counselling, military command, public worship, and the relation of divine law to civil authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Punishments
rubrics_metrics.description: The end of punishing is not revenge, and discharge of choler; but correction, either of the offender, or of others by his example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punishments should aim at correction and deterrence rather than vengeance; severity must be calibrated to achieve correction and to set an example for others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severity Applied to Most Dangerous Crimes
rubrics_metrics.description: The severest Punishments are to be inflicted for those Crimes, that are of most Danger to the Publique; such as are those which proceed from malice to the Government established; those that spring from contempt of Justice; those that provoke Indignation in the Multitude; and those, which unpunished, seem Authorised, as when they are committed by Sonnes, Servants, or Favorites of men in Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize harsh penalties for crimes that threaten public safety, the authority of government, public confidence in justice, or which would appear legitimized if left unpunished (especially offenses by relatives/servants/favorites of the powerful). Example: a single insolent act by a ruler's son that provokes indignation can topple a regime (Tarquin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lenity for Crimes of Infirmity
rubrics_metrics.description: Crimes of Infirmity; such as are those which proceed from great provocation, from great fear, great need, or from ignorance whether the Fact be a great Crime, or not, there is place many times for Lenity, without prejudice to the Common-wealth; and Lenity when there is such place for it, is required by the Law of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show mercy when wrongdoing arises from provocation, fear, necessity, or ignorance, provided leniency does not endanger the commonwealth. Distinguish willful malice from infirmity of circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punish Leaders, Not the Seduced
rubrics_metrics.description: The Punishment of the Leaders, and teachers in a Commotion; not the poore seduced People, when they are punished, can profit the Common-wealth by their example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target punishment at instigators and teachers of unrest rather than at the misled masses, since punishing victims teaches less and may be unjust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Rewards for Public Benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: It belongeth to the Office, and Duty of the Soveraign, to apply his Rewards alwayes so, as there may arise from them benefit to the Common-wealth: wherein consisteth their Use, and End; and is then done, when they that have well served the Common-wealth, are with as little expence of the Common Treasure, as is possible, so well recompenced, as others thereby may be encouraged...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design rewards to incentivize public service efficiently (maximise encouragement, minimise public expense). Rewards should reflect past service, not be payments for future silence or abandonment of opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do Not Buy Off Ambitious Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: To buy with Mony, or Preferment, from a Popular ambitious Subject, to be quiet, and desist from making ill impressions in the mindes of the People, has nothing of the nature of Reward ... nor does it tend to the Benefit, but to the Dammage of the Publique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rewarding would‑be troublemakers merely to secure their quiet: such payments promote imitation and increase malice by making mischief 'vendible' (Hydra metaphor). Prefer opposing early beginnings of ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of Counsellors — Merit and Disinterest
rubrics_metrics.description: The most able Counsellours, are they that have least hope of benefit by giving evill Counsell, and most knowledge of those things that conduce to the Peace, and Defence of the Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select advisers who are knowledgeable and have minimal personal stake in giving dishonest counsel. Avoid hereditary or inherited entitlement to council seats; prefer demonstrated competence and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs of Self‑interested Counsellors
rubrics_metrics.description: The signes that guide to a just suspicion, is the soothing of the people in their unreasonable, or irremediable grievances, by men whose estates are not sufficient to discharge their accustomed expences...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for advisers who flatter or soothe with unrealistic remedies, especially those whose own finances or ambitions make them likely to foment or exploit public trouble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs of Knowledgeable Counsellors
rubrics_metrics.description: The best signes of Knowledge of any Art, are, much conversing in it, and constant good effects of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess advisers by long experience in public affairs and a track record of practical, good results rather than by title or wealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of Giving Counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: The benefit of their Counsell is greater, when they give every one his Advice, and reasons of it apart, than when they do it in an Assembly, by way of Orations; and when they have praemeditated, than when they speak on the sudden...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel is more reliable when given in written/individual, premeditated form rather than impromptu speeches. This reduces influence of passions (envy, emulation) and improves deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Complaints as Source of Internal Policy Advice
rubrics_metrics.description: The best Counsell ... in those things that concern not other Nations, but onely the ease, and benefit the Subjects may enjoy, by Lawes that look onely inward, is to be taken from the generall informations, and complaints of the people of each Province, who are best acquainted with their own wants...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For internal, provincial matters, give weight to local information and complaints; locals best know their needs, provided requests don't conflict with essential sovereign rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commander Qualities for Military Success
rubrics_metrics.description: A Commander of an Army in chiefe ... must therefore be Industrious, Valiant, Affable, Liberall and Fortunate, that he may gain an opinion both of sufficiency, and of loving his Souldiers. This is Popularity, and breeds in the Souldiers both desire, and courage...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose commanders who combine competence (industrious, valiant), approachability (affable), generosity (liberal), and luck/fortune to inspire troops. Popularity in a commander motivates soldiers but can pose political risks if misaligned with sovereign authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Danger of Subject‑Popularity Without Sovereign Popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: But this love of Souldiers ... is a dangerous thing to Soveraign Power; especially when it is in the hands of an Assembly not popular. ... When the Soveraign himselfe is Popular ... there is no danger at all from the Popularity of a Subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure sovereign legitimacy and popularity to mitigate risk of powerful subordinates using troop loyalty for sedition; absent sovereign popularity, popular generals can threaten the state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of Nations equals Law of Nature for Sovereigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerning the Offices of one Soveraign to another, which are comprehended in that Law, which is commonly called the Law of Nations, I need not say any thing in this place; because the Law of Nations, and the Law of Nature, is the same thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat international duties between sovereigns as governed by the same natural principles that govern individuals; sovereigns have comparable rights to procure their people's safety as individuals have over their bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Are Subjects in the Kingdom of God
rubrics_metrics.description: They therefore that believe there is a God that governeth the world, and hath given Praecepts, and propounded Rewards, and Punishments to Mankind, are Gods Subjects; all the rest, are to be understood as Enemies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Hobbes' framework, being a 'subject' of divine rule depends on acknowledgement of divine governance and acceptance of its precepts (faith/hope/fear); denial of divine providence places one outside that moral‑political community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law Requires Promulgation to Remove Ignorance
rubrics_metrics.description: To rule by Words, requires that such Words be manifestly made known; for else they are no Lawes: For to the nature of Lawes belongeth a sufficient, and clear Promulgation, such as may take away the excuse of Ignorance...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laws (including divine laws) must be sufficiently promulgated and made known to remove excuses of ignorance; otherwise they do not function as law. This underpins the threefold manner God declares laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threefold Word of God and Corresponding Hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: God declareth his Lawes three wayes; by the Dictates of Naturall Reason, By Revelation, and by the Voyce of some Man, to whom by the operation of Miracles, he procureth credit with the rest. From hence there ariseth a triple Word of God, Rational, Sensible, and Prophetique: to which Correspondeth a triple Hearing; Right Reason, Sense Supernaturall, and Faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate modes of divine communication and their epistemic bases: natural reason (accessible to all), revelation/inspiration (private and particular), and prophetic/sensible miracles (to establish a mediator). Policy and obedience should respect the appropriate mode and its audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twofold Kingdom of God: Natural and Prophetical
rubrics_metrics.description: There may be attributed to God, a two-fold Kingdome, Naturall, and Prophetique: Naturall, wherein he governeth as many of Mankind as acknowledge his Providence, by the naturall Dictates of Right Reason; And Prophetique, wherein ... he governed them ... by Positive Lawes, which he gave them by the mouthes of his holy Prophets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between moral duties derivable by reason (natural kingdom) applicable universally, and special positive laws given to a chosen people (prophetical kingdom) which require different treatment in political practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes Proper to Divine Honour
rubrics_metrics.description: That we may know what worship of God is taught us by the light of Nature, I will begin with his Attributes ... Hee that will attribute to God, nothing but what is warranted by naturall Reason, must either use such Negative Attributes, as Infinite, Eternall, Incomprehensible; or Superlatives, as Most High, Most Great...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When ascribing attributes to God in worship, avoid finite, spatial, or passion‑based predicates; prefer negative, superlative, or indefinite terms (Infinite, Eternal, Most High) that express reverence without circumscribing divine nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions That Signify Divine Honour
rubrics_metrics.description: They be signes of the Intention to Honour God; such as are, First, Prayers ... Secondly, Thanksgiving ... Thirdly, Gifts; that is to say, Sacrifices, and Oblations ... Fourthly, Not to swear by any but God ... Fifthly, it is a part of Rationall Worship, to speak Considerately of God ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public and private acts of prayer, thanksgiving, offerings, exclusive oaths by God, and measured, reverent speech about God are proper signs of honour. These acts should be significant, composed, and sincere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and Mode of Worship
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a Dictate of naturall Reason, that they be every one in his kind the best, and most significant of Honour ... that Prayers, and Thanksgiving, be made in Words and Phrases, not sudden, nor light, nor Plebeian; but beautifull and well composed ... that the Beasts they offered in sacrifice ... were full of submission ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Worship acts should aim to be the best of their kind: composed language, appropriate sacrifices/gifts, full submission — form matters as an expression of honour. Public worship is especially important to encourage others to honour God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Worship Requires Uniformity
rubrics_metrics.description: But seeing a Common-wealth is but one Person, it ought also to exhibite to God but one Worship; which then it doth, when it commandeth it to be exhibited by Private men, Publiquely. ... the property whereof, is to be Uniforme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A commonwealth should command a single, uniform public worship to express its unity; allowing many public religions undermines a public religion and the state's unified identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil Authority Determines Arbitrary Signs of Worship
rubrics_metrics.description: Those Attributes which the Soveraign ordaineth, in the Worship of God, for signes of Honour, ought to be taken and used for such by private men in their publique Worship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil laws and sovereign decisions can prescribe arbitrary signs/gestures of public worship (e.g., rites, gestures) which subjects are then bound to observe in public practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of Human Power Over Natural Signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all Actions are signes by Constitution; but some are Naturally signes of Honour, others of Contumely, these later ... cannot be made by humane power a part of Divine worship; nor the former ... ever be separated from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human authority cannot convert naturally honourable actions into dishonourable ones or vice versa; some expressions of honour (e.g., modest behaviour, prayer) are inherently bound to worship and cannot be wholly legislated away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural Punishments as Consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no action of man in this life, that is not the beginning of so long a chayn of Consequences ... Intemperance, is naturally punished with Diseases; Rashnesse, with Mischances; Injustice, with the Violence of Enemies; Pride, with Ruine; Cowardise, with Oppression; Negligent government of Princes, with Rebellion; and Rebellion, with Slaughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that moral and political failures produce natural chains of consequences; anticipate and weigh long‑term natural punishments when judging actions/policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of Prophetic Word in Christian Politics (with Reason retained)
rubrics_metrics.description: Of Christian Politiques: The Word Of God Delivered By Prophets Is The Main Principle ... Neverthelesse, we are not to renounce our Senses, and Experience; nor ... our naturall Reason. For they are the talents which he hath put into our hands ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a Christian commonwealth, prophetic revelation is primary for political doctrine, but revelation must be interpreted alongside sense, experience, and natural reason; do not abandon reason in governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captivity of the Understanding (Submission of Will)
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Captivity of our Understanding, is not meant a Submission of the Intellectual faculty, to the Opinion of any other man; but of the Will to Obedience ... We then Captivate our Understanding and Reason, when we forbear contradiction; when we so speak, as (by lawfull Authority) we are commanded; and when we live accordingly; which in sum, is Trust, and Faith reposed in him that speaketh...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authority legitimately requires obedience (e.g., divine precepts as delivered by lawful interpreters), submission consists in the will (forbearance of contradiction and lawful outward compliance) rather than forced change of intellectual faculties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private Immediate Revelations Do Not Bind Others
rubrics_metrics.description: When God speaketh to a man immediately ... if a man pretend to me, that God hath spoken to him supernaturally, and immediately, and I make doubt of it, I cannot easily perceive what argument he can produce, to oblige me to beleeve it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private, immediate claims of divine speech by individuals do not obligate others to belief or obedience; only mediated, publicly recognized prophetic authority (Scripture/Church) can ground public obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scripture as Mediated Divine Speech
rubrics_metrics.description: For to say that God hath spoken to him in the Holy Scripture, is not to say God hath spoken to him immediately, but by mediation of the Prophets, or of the Apostles, or of the Church...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Scripture and recognized prophetic/apostolic/Church mediation as the legitimate public channel for divine commands binding the Christian commonwealth; distinguish private inspiration from public revelation.
